To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the mortality rate after reoperation is higher than after first time surgery, and that it is highest in the early period following reoperation (the 30 days immediately following reoperation) and decreases over time.
the mortality rate for reoperation after CABG is approximately 3.5%, and the risk for reoperation increases with age and the number of prior CABG operations.
the risk of death after coronary bypass reoperation (CBR) is 2.5 times higher than after the first operation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the long-term effects of the use of a new technology in a new application.
a study of the medical and economic consequences of coronary bypass reoperation.
the identification of risk factors for reoperations in the first 10 years following coronary bypass surgery.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
reoperative coronary bypass surgery (CBPS) is a safe, effective and necessary operation for patients with coronary disease who have previously undergone CBPS and have recurrent angina.
there is a statistically significant difference in the mortality rates of reoperative and non-reoperative patients.
the risk of reoperation is not significantly different than the risk of original CABG.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mortality rate for coronary bypass reoperation is 2.5% and the morbidity rate is 15%.
the 15-year survival rate of the first 1,500 patients who underwent reoperation for recurrent coronary artery disease (CAD) at the Cleveland Clinic is 75%.
reoperation after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) is a major challenge.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mortality risk for coronary bypass reoperation is much greater than the risk for the original procedure.
the risk of death after coronary artery reoperations (CABR) is much lower than the risk of death for the first CABG.
reoperation after coronary artery bypass grafting (re-CABG) is not the death sentence it used to be.
